title: Sofa 2026-08-05 — reconstruction benchmark
lede: One subject, one day, five reconstructions. The same tan leather sofa, captured as 31 photos and a 356-frame video, through generative (TRELLIS), photogrammetry (Meshroom/AliceVision) and an open-source reproduction of the KIRI Engine pipeline. All metric, gravity-aligned, measurable in-viewer. The RGB-D fuse rows were retired: they measured the room, not the sofa.

cards.title: TRELLIS — PHOTO
cards.scale: metric via RGB-D dims (1917 x 2184 x 1651 mm)
cards.note: Fastest, cleanest, most complete-looking. Geometry is invented where unseen — complete, not measured.

cards.title: TRELLIS — VIDEO
cards.scale: metric via RGB-D dims (1206 x 1606 x 2127 mm)
cards.note: Same model, views drawn from video. Its dims differ from the photo run because the RGB-D fuse it borrows from differs.

cards.title: Meshroom — PHOTO
cards.scale: METRIC via ARKit camera track (residual 23 mm)
cards.note: 1.30M faces, 32.6k landmarks. Scaled+uprighted by aligning its 31 SfM camera centres to the session's metric ARKit poses.

cards.title: Meshroom — VIDEO
cards.scale: METRIC via ARKit camera track (residual 20 mm)
cards.note: 2.22M faces, 125k landmarks, single component. Same ARKit alignment over 150 cameras.

cards.title: KIRI-OSS — PHOTO
cards.method: open-source reproduction of KIRI's documented pipeline
cards.input: 31 photos (28 kept by a fixed 90% quota)
cards.scale: METRIC, isolated — 81 x 34 x 35 in ± 1–2 in
cards.note: BiRefNet masking + AliceVision, scaled by fitting the RGB-only camera track onto the ARKit track (RMS 30 mm, per-camera median 24 mm, worst 70 mm). The only row whose scale is solved on geometry isolated to the sofa — the RGB-D fuse measures a room, TRELLIS borrows one axis of those numbers, Meshroom stays in SfM units. Two caveats: H is a STANDING height, mesh top to the LiDAR floor plane, so ~10 in of it is the gap under a sofa whose legs the isolation removed (the mesh you can load is 25 in tall); and 76% of its surface lies within 20 mm of the LiDAR depth while only 34% of the LiDAR surface lies within 20 mm of it — locally accurate, substantially incomplete.
cards.caveat: H is measured to the LiDAR floor — the mesh you can load here is 25 in tall.
